result.judge_notes: pass 1 (A=with, B=without): A gives a clear ranking of all four audiences and explains it: landowners come second because losing access ends a race. It proposes checking the runners-first guess against entrant 'how did you hear' sources the organizers already collect, and its cuts each come with a reason, plus an owner and freshness table. B has a slightly fuller week-by-week plan, but it lumps sponsors and landowners together instead of ranking them. Its check ('look at analytics or just ask yourselves') is vaguer, and it states a few unsupported claims as fact, such as runners making up the mailing list and generic tips doing little. | pass 2 (A=without, B=with): B ranks all four audiences explicitly, with a sharp reason for putting landowners second (losing access ends a race). It treats 'runners come first' as a guess to check against entrant-source data the organizers already collect, and it gives a short per-audience needs table. A is also decisive and well sequenced, but it lumps sponsors and landowners together, its content lists read more like an inventory, and its check depends on analytics they may not have.
